question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `plugin-sdk/archive`, `plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `plugin-sdk/secret-file` as supported external plugin APIs in this filesystem refactor?
rationale: These subpaths add new public plugin contracts that external plugins may adopt, so implementation correctness alone cannot decide their long-term compatibility and ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve the focused SDK contracts
options.body: Keep the three subpaths after confirming they are the intended stable plugin boundary, then complete dependency publication and frozen-install proof.

options.title: Keep helpers core-only
options.body: Remove the new public subpaths and migrate bundled callers through existing internal or already-approved SDK seams.

options.title: Defer the API decision
options.body: Keep the PR draft until a maintainer defines the supported filesystem capability boundary for external plugins.

recommendation.title: Approve the focused SDK contracts
recommendation.body: Keep the three subpaths after confirming they are the intended stable plugin boundary, then complete dependency publication and frozen-install proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked fs-safe work and the branch’s dependency and SDK-boundary commits make steipete the clearest technical participant to provide the implementation context for the maintainer decision.
